title: Data-model, sharing, automation, and integration whiteboard exercises
objectives: Whiteboard a Salesforce slice that includes data model, sharing, automation, and integration—not only boxes.
Choose lookup versus master-detail and OWD with a spoken reason, marking edition gates Needs verification.
Pick one automation path using official which-tool guidance.
Add an integration contract: identity, direction, volume, errors—not a logo.
diagnostic_question: Legal must review large Opportunities and their system of record is an external CLM. On a whiteboard, how do you show objects, who sees legal text, what runs on Closed Won, and how Salesforce talks to CLM?
definition: Data-model, sharing, automation, and integration whiteboard exercises are timed designs where you draw those four layers together. Objects and fields come from the Object Reference mindset (object/field/record). Sharing is org-wide defaults and beyond. Automation follows Which Tool. Integration is a contract, guided by Well-Architected Trusted/Easy/Adaptable and architect Decision Guides—not a vendor sticker. ([Object Reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_concepts.htm); [Which tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Record-triggered guide](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/record-triggered); [Well-Architected](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview))
why_it_matters: A pretty ERD that ignores sharing fails architect and senior-admin loops. A sharing model with no automation path fails too. Whiteboards are how interviewers see whether you can hold four concerns at once.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat the whiteboard like a city-planning board. Zoning is the data model: what parcels exist. Access roads are sharing: who can enter which parcel. Traffic lights are automation: what happens when a car arrives. Highways to the next city are integration: identity at the on-ramp, direction of traffic, volume, and what happens when a truck breaks down. A map with only zoning is not a city.
deeper_explanation: Object Reference frames object, field, and record as table/column/row structurally—not as authorization. Whiteboard the nouns first, then say what is standard versus custom. ([Object Reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_concepts.htm))

Sharing Help documents org-wide defaults as the baseline access for records a user does not own. You must speak OWD, then roles, sharing rules, or teams as needed—without inventing a default. ([OWD](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd.htm); [Sharing overview](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_overview.htm))

Which-tool Help plus the record-triggered automation Decision Guide keep the automation lane honest: one primary path, not three hidden Flows and a trigger. ([Which tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Record-triggered](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/record-triggered))

Well-Architected Trusted (security, reliability) and Adaptable (interoperability) discipline the integration highway. Architect career path points at Decision Guides. ([Well-Architected](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview); [Architect path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/architect))

Application Architect orientation emphasizes native features, data, and sharing—start there before drawing middleware. ([Application Architect](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/applicationarchitect))

mental_model.analogy: City-planning board: zoning (data model), access roads (sharing), traffic lights (automation), highways to the next city (integration).
useful_mapping: objects/fields → zoning parcels and building types
OWD and sharing → who may enter which road
named credential / inbound API → highway on-ramp identity
volume and errors → trucks per hour and tow trucks
logo without a contract → drawing a neighboring city with no road
where_it_breaks: Orgs are not cities; Experience Cloud users are not 'tourists' in a legal sense.
Master-detail cascade is not a zoning law you should invent—verify current object-relationship docs.
You cannot draw every sharing feature in 20 minutes; say what you omitted.
Planning-board analogy is not a Salesforce product.

teach_back_prompt: Draw four quadrants—data, sharing, automation, integration—for the legal-plus-CLM scenario. Speak one decision in each.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory, restate the core terms and one clarifying question you would ask.
Classify four realistic interview signals using this topic's decision table.
Teach the analogy, then name two places it breaks.
Walk one troubleshooting symptom from evidence to next action.
Give a two-minute interview answer without notes, then one follow-up.

claims.claim: Salesforce Object Reference describes objects, fields, and records as the structural units of data (table/column/row as a structural analogy).
Organization-wide defaults define baseline access to records the user does not own.
Sharing architecture includes more than OWD; overview Help describes the sharing model layers.
Automation on the whiteboard should follow official which-tool guidance and the record-triggered Decision Guide rather than stacking hidden automations.
Well-Architected and Application Architect orientation push native data/sharing skill and interoperability without treating a vendor logo as a design.
claims.validation: Well-Architected, AA credential, architect career path.

Integration pattern catalog names should be re-read from current Decision Guides before quoting a specific pattern title.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I draw four lanes: data model, sharing, automation, and integration. Nouns first, OWD next, one automation path, then identity and errors if another system exists. I do not paste a logo and call it architecture.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with Opportunity plus a private Legal_Review__c if comments are sensitive. I say OWD is baseline for records you do not own and I pick private on the child. Automation: validation or before-save for the freeze; callouts are not that tool. If CLM is system of record, Salesforce is not the legal noun—I draw direction, named credential or inbound auth, volume, and failure. I say what I omitted. I mark relationship cascade rules Needs verification rather than inventing them.

terminology.precise: Objects and fields as schema metadata; records as instances—Object Reference structural view.
terminology.non_example: Drawing only 'cloud' bubbles with no API names.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: ERD: a notation; this lane is the Salesforce mapping.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent roll-up limit numbers.

terminology.precise: OWD as baseline for non-owned records, then role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, or implicit parent access as needed.
terminology.example: Legal_Review__c OWD Private; Opportunity stays whatever the org uses, with FLS on any leftover fields.
terminology.non_example: A lock icon with no OWD words.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: FLS: field visibility, complementary, not a substitute for record sharing.
terminology.boundary: Do not guess the org's current Opportunity OWD; ask or assume explicitly.

terminology.plain: What runs when data changes or a user clicks.
terminology.precise: One primary path using which-tool and record-triggered guidance.
terminology.example: Validation rule blocking Closed Won without an approved review.
terminology.non_example: Three Flows, a Process Builder, and a trigger all stamping the same field.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Order of execution: later APEX/AUTO topic; mention it exists, do not recite unofficial lists.
terminology.boundary: Callouts do not belong in before-save Flow.

terminology.plain: How Salesforce and another system share work.
terminology.precise: Identity, direction (in/out), volume, error handling, and which system is source of truth.
terminology.example: CLM owns the contract PDF; Salesforce stores a status and external id; nightly or event-driven sync with named credentials.
terminology.non_example: A MuleSoft logo in the corner.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Outbound message: one older option, not the whole lane.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent API rate limits.

terminology.plain: Which system is allowed to win on a noun.
terminology.precise: Whiteboard truth: if CLM is SoR for legal documents, do not also model a competing full document object without a sync rule.
terminology.example: CLM SoR for clauses; Salesforce SoR for Opportunity stage.
terminology.non_example: Two SoRs with no conflict rule.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Master-detail: a Salesforce relationship, not 'master' as SoR.
terminology.boundary: Say the conflict rule out loud.

terminology.plain: How tightly two objects share life and security.
terminology.precise: Interview must give a reason (ownership, roll-ups, cascade) and mark cascade/roll-up details Needs verification.
terminology.example: Lookup from Legal_Review__c to Opportunity so reviews can exist with tighter sharing than the parent.
terminology.non_example: Master-detail by habit because 'it is a child.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Hierarchical relationship: special User lookup, out of scope.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent cascade-delete behavior; verify.

terminology.plain: A fact you stated because the prompt omitted it.
terminology.precise: Whiteboards require labeled assumptions: volume, licenses, current OWD.
terminology.example: Assume 200 Opportunities/day and internal users only, written in a corner.
terminology.non_example: Silent assumptions the interviewer cannot grade.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Constraint: a given from the prompt, not an assumption.
terminology.boundary: Wrong assumptions are cheaper than invented platform limits.

terminology.plain: What you did not draw for time.
terminology.precise: Senior move: 'I am not drawing territory management' rather than pretending the map is complete.
terminology.example: No Experience Cloud on this 20-minute board.
terminology.non_example: Leaving sharing blank and hoping they do not notice.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Parking lot: a list of follow-ups.
terminology.boundary: Do not omit sharing entirely; omit advanced features with a note.

mechanics.after: Which nouns live in Salesforce vs CLM
mechanics.failure: Duplicate legal document objects with no rule

mechanics.after: Standard vs custom, lookup vs MD with a reason
mechanics.failure: Invented cascade rules stated as fact

mechanics.transition: Add sharing and one automation path
Add integration contract or explicitly skip

when_to_use: When an architect or senior interview is a data-model, sharing, automation, and integration whiteboard exercise.
When you must show OWD as baseline access, not a lock doodle.
When the prompt includes an external system of record and you need a contract, not a logo.
When automation choice must follow which-tool and record-triggered guidance on the board.
When you need to label assumptions and omissions in 20 minutes.
when_not_to_use: Do not spend the whole whiteboard on an ERD and skip sharing, automation, and integration.
Do not invent roll-up, cascade, or API-limit numbers on the board.
Do not draw three automations on the same field because it looks thorough.
Do not treat a vendor logo as the integration lane.
Do not whiteboard using real customer confidential schemas in a public interview recording.
configuration_or_code_location: Object Reference and Sharing Help as crib notes (not during a closed-book interview unless allowed)
Which-tool Help and record-triggered Decision Guide
No production Setup during the exercise

worked_example.scenario: Twenty-minute data-model, sharing, automation, and integration whiteboard: legal reviews large Opportunities; contract language lives in an external CLM; sales still closes in Salesforce. Internal users only. You must cover all four lanes.
inputs: CLM is system of record for contract documents
Legal comments must not be widely readable

decisions.decision: Salesforce objects: Opportunity (standard) + Legal_Review__c lookup child with status; no competing PDF store.
decisions.because: CLM remains SoR for documents; Salesforce stores review status and external id.

decisions.decision: Sharing: Legal_Review__c OWD Private; FLS so sales cannot read comments; automation: validation on Closed Won; integration: outbound status to CLM with named credential, daily volume assumption, error queue.
decisions.because: Four lanes, one path each, identity and errors spoken.
decisions.rejected: Public Opportunity field plus a MuleSoft logo

configuration_or_code: Corner assumptions: internal users, 200 opps/day, Opportunity OWD unknown—will verify.
Callout: cascade/roll-up behavior Needs verification if they insist on master-detail.
worked_example.output: A four-lane board the interviewer can photograph: nouns, OWD, one freeze, one contract.
verification: Each lane has one spoken decision.
SoR is labeled on CLM for documents.
worked_example.self_explanation: City-planning board: zoning, roads, lights, highway—without pretending the map is the whole country.

hands_on_lab.environment: Paper or a drawing app. Optional playground only to verify OWD labels, not to build the whole design.
steps: Divide the page into four quadrants: data, sharing, automation, integration.
Draw two objects and one relationship with a lookup-versus-MD reason.
Write an OWD for the sensitive object and one FLS note.
Write one automation tool and one integration identity/direction/error line.
List two omissions and one Needs verification.
guided_completion: Read the integration line without saying a vendor logo
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Repeat with Experience Cloud partners added; show what changes in sharing and integration.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Relationship cascade details are Needs verification. Decision Guide pages may be reorganized.

decision_table.signal: Sensitive text must not follow Opportunity visibility
decision_table.choose: Private child object plus FLS; speak OWD as baseline for non-owned records
decision_table.why: Sharing lane exists so data-model convenience does not leak legal comments

decision_table.signal: Same-record Closed Won freeze, no callout
decision_table.choose: Validation rule or before-save Flow as the one automation path
decision_table.not: Trigger plus two Flows plus Process Builder on Stage
decision_table.why: Which-tool and record-triggered guidance prefer one primary path

decision_table.signal: External CLM is system of record for documents
decision_table.choose: Salesforce stores status and external id; draw identity, direction, volume, errors
decision_table.not: Duplicate PDFs in Salesforce and a vendor logo
decision_table.why: Integration lane is a contract; Well-Architected interoperability is not a sticker

decision_table.choose: Skip the highway and say so
decision_table.not: Draw middleware anyway to look senior

decision_table.signal: You do not know cascade-delete rules for master-detail
decision_table.choose: Choose lookup or mark cascade Needs verification
decision_table.why: Interviewers prefer honest verification over folklore

limitations: You cannot draw the entire sharing architecture in 20 minutes.
Pattern names in Decision Guides can change.
OWD for standard objects is org-specific.
security_notes: Named credentials beat hardcoded secrets in the integration lane.
Do not photograph real customer org schemas.

check: Did you time-box each lane to 5 minutes?

troubleshooting.symptom: Interviewer asked 'who sees this?' and you had nothing
check: Recover; do not defend the miss

production_notes: After the interview, verify OWD and licenses in a sandbox before building.
Whiteboard is not a deploy plan.
Record assumptions in the design doc if you are hired to build it.

interview_questions.question: How do you structure a data-model, sharing, automation, and integration whiteboard?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Four lanes with time-boxes. Nouns and SoR, OWD, one automation path, then a contract or an omission. No logos as architecture.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I divide the board. Data model uses object/field/record language. Sharing starts at OWD. Automation uses which-tool so I do not stack Flows. Integration is identity, direction, volume, errors. I write assumptions. I mark cascade rules Needs verification.
interview_questions.example: Opportunity plus private Legal_Review__c, validation freeze, CLM status sync.
follow_ups: What if they only wanted ERD?

interview_questions.question: How do you talk sharing on a whiteboard without boiling the ocean?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I state OWD as baseline for non-owned records, pick a default for the sensitive object, then name the next layer I would add if needed.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not draw every sharing feature. I will not guess the org's Opportunity OWD—I assume or ask. FLS is on the board for legal fields. I mention role hierarchy or sharing rules as the next knob. I omit territory with a note if time dies.
interview_questions.example: Legal_Review__c Private; Opportunity OWD unknown-verify; FLS hides comments from sales.
weak_answer_warnings: Claiming OWD is an Apex modifier

interview_questions.question: Legal plus external CLM. Walk the four lanes in two minutes.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Salesforce owns stage; CLM owns documents; private review child; validation freeze; sync status with named credentials and an error path.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Data: Opportunity + Legal_Review__c lookup, external id. Sharing: private child. Automation: block Closed Won without approve—no callout in before-save. Integration: CLM SoR, outbound or inbound, volume assumption, dead-letter. Omissions: Experience Cloud, territory.
interview_questions.example: Status field plus CLM id; PDF not stored in Salesforce.
weak_answer_warnings: Duplicate PDF library in Salesforce with no SoR

interview_questions.question: The interviewer hands you only an ERD template. How do you still cover automation and integration?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I annotate the ERD with OWD, a numbered automation path, and a side contract box, even if the template had no swimlanes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Templates are not the exercise. I write (1) validation on Stage (2) Private OWD on child (3) named credential to CLM. If they insist on more entities, I add them after the four decisions. I will not fill 12 objects and skip sharing.
interview_questions.example: Sticky notes on an ERD: OWD, Flow/validation, API direction.
follow_ups: What if they stop you adding notes?
How tiny can the contract box be?

interview_questions.question: They ask who sees legal comments and your board is blank. Recover.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I add the sharing lane now: OWD, FLS, and who-must-not-see, and I acknowledge the miss.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Recovery scores. I do not pretend I covered it. I pick Private on the child and FLS on any parent leftovers. I ask about partners. I do not invent their current Opportunity OWD.
interview_questions.example: Quick box: Legal_Review__c Private; sales FLS none on Comments__c.

interview_questions.question: You stacked two Flows and a trigger on Stage. They look unhappy. Recover.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I pick one primary path, park the others, and cite which-tool / record-triggered guidance.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I say stacked automation is an Easy/maintainability failure. I keep the validation freeze and delete the extra stamps from the board. I mention order-of-execution exists but I will not reciting unofficial lists. I offer Apex only if a callout remains.
interview_questions.example: One validation rule left on the board; trigger erased.
follow_ups: What if production already has all three?
How do you sequence a cleanup?

interview_questions.question: When would you put legal documents in Salesforce instead of CLM?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When Salesforce is truly SoR—or a thin copy with a conflict rule—not by default because we like Files.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If they have no CLM, Files plus a private library and sharing may be enough. If CLM exists, I do not compete. If they need Salesforce search, I design a sync with SoR still on CLM. I mark file-storage limits Needs verification. Integration lane still has identity and errors.
interview_questions.example: No-CLM org: ContentDocument linked to Legal_Review__c with tight library sharing—verify Files features.
follow_ups: What Help would you open after?

interview_questions.question: Teach the city-planning analogy for this whiteboard and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Zoning, roads, lights, highways. It breaks because orgs are not cities and you cannot draw the whole country in 20 minutes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Parcels are objects, buildings are records, roads are sharing, lights are automation, highways are integration with on-ramp identity. A zoning-only map fails. It breaks on Experience Cloud, on invented cascade 'laws,' and on logos that are not roads. I then draw the four quadrants for legal plus CLM.
interview_questions.example: Private child, validation freeze, CLM contract line.
